AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: Mortality after hospitalization with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) is high, compared with age-matched controls. Available evidence suggests a strong link with cardiovascular disease. Our aim was to explore the prognostic value of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (cTnT) for mortality in patients hospitalized with CAP.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: CTnT level on admission was measured (assay conducted in 2015) in 295 patients hospitalized with CAP who participated in a randomized placebo-controlled double-blind trial on adjunctive dexamethasone treatment. Outcome measures were short- (30-day) and long-term (4.1-year) mortalities.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: CTnT levels were elevated (≥14 ng/L) in 132 patients (45%). Pneumonia severity index (PSI) class was 4-5 in 137 patients (46%). Short- and long-term mortality were significantly higher in patients with elevated cTnT levels. cTnT level on admission combined with PSI classification was significantly better in predicting short-term mortality (area under the operating curve (AUC) = 0.903; 95% CI = 0.847-0.960), compared with PSI classification alone (AUC = 0.818; 95% CI = 0.717-0.919). An optimal cTnT cut-off level of 28 ng/L was independently associated with both short- and long-term mortality (OR = 21.9; 95% CI = 4.7-101.4 and 10.7; 95% CI = 5.0-22.8, respectively).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Elevated cTnT level on admission is a strong predictor of short- and long-term mortalities in patients hospitalized with CAP.
